speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin. To determine the cause, how many days old are you, and when did you first notice this jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the jaundice is progressing rapidly and you've noted no changes in stool or urine, have you noticed the baby is passing stool, and if so, what is its color? Also, has the baby been urinating at least 6 times in the last 24 hours? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_Level (Total and Direct).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby has passed meconium and is urinating normally, and I have requested your bilirubin levels. The absence of pale stools or dark urine helps rule out biliary atresia, but the rapid progression from face to trunk is concerning. While we await the lab results, can you confirm if the baby is feeding well and gaining weight appropriately?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born full term at 38 weeks via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. No past medical history. Social history: Exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the history of exclusive breastfeeding, full-term gestation, and the absence of stool or urine changes, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Breast Milk Jaundice. To confirm this and rule out hemolysis, I need your immediate results for the Bilirubin test we ordered. Did you notice any bruising or bleeding on the baby's skin? DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice
